title: Frontier Town
paragraphs: Western adventure about lawyer Chad Remington, who returns to the frontier town of Dos Rios and becomes a crime-fighting attorney in a community caught between the old West and a new legal order.

Syndicated Western legal-adventure series built around Chad Remington and Cherokee O’Bannon in Dos Rios. The 48-object GRH container represents 47 underlying numbered stories plus one exact duplicate archive copy of program #2. Multiple syndication schedules are preserved separately.
GRH documents the program through Original documented syndication schedule (March 5, 1949 to January 21, 1950) and Later GRH syndication schedule (September 26, 1952 to August 14, 1953).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Bruce Eells (producer on 48 recordings), Paul Franklin (director on 48 recordings and writer on 48 recordings), Wade Crosby (performer on 48 recordings), Bill Forman (announcer on 46 recordings), Ivan Ditmars (organist on 39 recordings, composer on 4 recordings, conductor on 4 recordings, and performer on 2 recordings), [[person|reed-hadley|Reed Hadley]] (performer on 26 recordings), and [[person|jeff-chandler|Jeff Chandler]] (performer on 22 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include western frontier community, law, courts and frontier justice, outlaws, robbery and violent crime, land, homesteading and property conflict, cattle, ranching and trail drives, and railroads, stages and transport.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Transcription syndication and local commercial insertion, Multiple market/distribution chronologies, and Frontier law and legal-order storytelling.
